recipes.name: Basil Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 3 tablespoons Dijon mustard (such as Grey Poupon Country Mustard™)
3 pounds fresh shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: In a shallow, non-porous dish or bowl, mix together olive oil and melted butter. Stir in lemon juice, mustard, basil, and garlic, and season with salt and white pepper. Add shrimp, and toss to coat. Cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat grill to high heat. Remove shrimp from marinade, and thread onto skewers. Discard marinade.
Lightly oil grill grate, and arrange skewers on preheated grill. Cook for 4 minutes, turning once, or until opaque.

raw_recipe.headline: Basil Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: This mixture of basil, lemon juice, mustard and garlic adds a wonderful texture and flavor to grilled shrimp. You won 't want to prepare them any other way.

review.reviewBody: Reduce the brown mustard, but most of all... Don't marinade for a whole hour! Shrimp (and all seafood for that matter) actually starts to cook when it sits in citrus juice. It doesn't need marinading more than 15-20 minutes!! Otherwise you will end up with tough, chewy shrimp.
Great flavor! For a twist, I marinate in a casserole dish, throw some canned tomatoes on top, and bake in the oven at 350 for 15-20 minutes. A nice, easy base to toss with pasta or rice.

Yum! Everyone love these shrimp. I did change a few things. I air fried the shrimp and tossed the marinade in the frying pan and reduced it. I also made a garlic white wine cream for my pasta and mixed it with the marinade just before serving and used a little to too off the shrimp. It was a hit

this was so delicious! i cut the recipe in half and used it on a little over a pound of shrimp.. i used all oil, lime instead of lemon, regular mustard, and dried basil.. doubled the garlic by accident.. marinated for about 20 minutes and cooked the shrimp in the marinade on my stovetop.. scooped the shrimp out and cooked some cauliflower florets in the broth.. it was to die for.. i literally licked my plate clean.. ty so much for the recipe ~UPDATE: this time i stuck a little more closely to the recipe.. i cut this down to 3 servings and used 1 T each of olive oil, dijon mustard, and bottled lemon juice.. left out the butter.. used 1/2 t kosher salt (will do 1/4 next time) and a couple of shakes of black pepper.. only had dried basil so used 2 t.. would love to try the fresh stuff.. marinated for 15-20 mins.. bf grilled these on the gas grill on our Island Grillstone.. the end result tasted pretty good but i wanted an acid on the end.. i dipped them in greek yogurt.. fresh lemon would be optimal.. ty again for the recipe
Great marinade. Loved the mustard affect though I only used 1 tablespoon due to picker eaters. Sauteed on the stove rather than cooked on the grill. Delicious.

Note: This is a review of the original recipe, but I did something different with the finished dish that some may like.
I did cut down the dijon mustard by half and grilled the marinated shrimp without skewers on a stove top grill. But instead of discarding the leftover marinade: Put it in a 10" saute pan and add 2 tbs butter, 2 tbs olive oil, (as much minced garlic as you like), and 1 1/2 cups medium chop roma tomatoes (without seeds). Cook up 3-4 portions of spaghetti. Heat sauce/tomatoes through, drain spaghetti and add to pan, then add grilled shrimp and mix it all together. Serve w/grated romano, parm, etc. and garnish with whole, small basil leaves. Yum. Thanks for the recipe!

This was really a great recipe- the marinade is so flavorful! I think I was short on the mustard by 1 tbs but it didn’t need all of it anyway. I only marinated the shrimp for about 15 mins and that was enough since the lemon juice started to cook the shrimp. The marinade smelled soo good that I decided to boil it on the stovetop for 10 mins so I could use it as a sauce for the mini red potatoes I had boiled and then grilled to go with the shrimp. Now that was amazing! I would double the recipe next time just to have more of that dreamy sauce. My friends and hubby raved about it.

I loved it! Trying to make a quick supper with ingredients at hand. Didn't want to grill. Put sauce together. Pan fried shrimp. Made pasta. Put shrimp on top then poured sauce over. Added some Frank's extra red hot and parmesan

Instead of using the grill, I put the marinade in a skillet to cook with the shrimp. Used it as a marinade, so I thickened it with cornstarch and served over rice. It was a HIT! The only problem is there weren't any left overs :)
I actually only used a couple tbsp of the butter and a Carolina BBQ sauce instead of mustard and sauteed it. It was great. cooked the sauce with Basil for a couple of mins and then added the shrimp.

It was very good! I hate making changes although ,,,, I kept the marinade and boiled it and added herb and garlic cream cheese. I served pasta mixed in the leftover marinade with the shrimp ....So good!
With all these ingredients it didn’t add up to much of a flavor.
So good! I followed the recipe exactly, but put in the oven at 400 degrees for 8 min. Such a quick and delicious meal.
Liked it, didn't love it, but it was OK and easy to make.
Reduced the lemon juice and mustard as recommended by others, and it came out great. Super easy and flavorful.

I followed the recipe exactly, and was rewarded with an easy-to-make, restaurant-quality main course. I served it with grilled corn on the cob, French fries, and Caprese Salad. Next time I’m going to make garlic-basil smashed potatoes using the excess marinade, instead of discarding it.
I’ve made this 3 times now and loved it every time! I added some soy sauce to the marinade for additional salt. Top notch recipe!!!

Sorry. I changed the recipe out of laziness and looking at other recipes. I put all the ingredients (except the mustard since I didn’t have any) into a large skillet. I did not melt the butter first but just put the chunk into the center. Then I put the shrimp all around and let it sit in it that marinade until my rice was cooked. I threw in 1/2 can, drained, diced tomatoes and sprinkled a bit cayenne pepper over the shrimp. When my veggies were almost finished, I fired up the stove to high. When the shrimp started to turn pink I flipped them and cooked them a bit more. Then I removed the shrimp and cooked down the sauce and poured it ontop. It was quick and really delicious.
